newsitem.title: USA: Spiegel CEO, president Shea to retire.
newsitem.headline: Spiegel CEO, president Shea to retire.

text.p: Spiegel Inc, which posted a loss in the first quarter and has launched an overhaul of its flagship catalog, said Friday president and chief executive John Shea would take early retirement.
Shea, whose retirement was to be effective July 3, had planned to leave the company next March on his 60th birthday, the company said.

But Shea decided now was an appropriate time to leave because the expansion of Spiegel's Eddie Bauer division has been successful and a reorganization of its flagship Spiegel catalog already was underway, Spiegel said in a statement.
Spiegel said it formed an office of the president including three existing Spiegel executives.

Harold Dahlstrand, a board member and senior vice president of human resources, was to serve as chairman of the office of president, Spiegel said. Michael Moran, general counsel, and James Sievers, chief financial officer, also were named to the office.
Last year, Spiegel lost $13.4 million, or $0.12 a share. During the first quarter, the company's loss more than doubled to $31 million, or $0.28 a share.
In April, the company said it would overhaul the merchandise offerings and the layout of its Spiegel catalog.

John Irvin will remain president and chief executive of Spiegel catalog, the company said. Likewise, Richard Fersch and George Ittner will remain president and chief executive of the company's Eddie Bauer and Newport News units respectively, Spiegel said.
